concepts: Siva, as the Lord and as the state the freed soul becomes
the Lord's holy feet, as refuge, as what the guru places on the disciple's head, and as the attainment itself
the body, as a perishable and impure frame
the Lord's grace, as distinct from compassion between beings
liberating knowledge, and the ஞானி who has it
yoga: the discipline of union with Siva, and the yogi who practises it
the spiritual teacher, whose path and feet lead to release
Shakti: the Lord's power, his consort, through whom he creates and acts
women who draw no line; women who sell intimacy
tattva: one of the (traditionally 36) constituents of the soul's world
God; the Lord, in the Kural usually named only by epithet
release; liberation from the cycle of births
perception of what is truly so
prana: the breath as life-force, and its control (pranayama) in yoga
the union of lovers, physical and emotional
impurity; the bonds (traditionally three) that bind the soul

avastha: a state of the soul's consciousness, chiefly waking (நனவு, சாக்கிரம்), dream (கனவு), deep sleep (சுழுத்தி), turiya (துரியம்) and the beyond (அதீதம்), each in Tirumular divided into the others and matched to tattvas, malas and places in the body
life; the life-breath at stake in love
bliss, especially the bliss of Siva (சிவானந்தம்) known in union with him, as distinct from worldly pleasure
mantra: the sacred formula, received from a guru, and the verses of the Tirumanthiram itself
infatuation; the deluded fascination of desire, the poet's word for his own state before the Lord's grace
maya: the material cause of bodies and worlds; also illusion
the Lord's devotees, his servants, as a community to be revered
pasu: the bound soul, one of the three Saiva Siddhanta categories with pati (the Lord) and pasam (the bonds)
Siva's holy dance in the hall (அம்பலம்) at Chidambaram, as the five acts, as letters and mantra, and as a dance within the body
love as sickness; the pain of longing
bindu: in cosmology the source of sound and form (mahamaya); in the body the seminal essence
nada: primal sound, paired with bindu as the first stage of manifestation
attainment; the powers that come with yoga, and the siddha who has them
pasam: the bonds that hold the soul, one of the three Saiva Siddhanta categories with pati and pasu
Tamil, as a language of revelation beside Sanskrit, and the poet's medium
a religious sect or system, often in Tirumular a source of delusion
the five-letter mantra of Siva (சிவாயநம, நமசிவாய and its other orders), the அஞ்செழுத்து
the eyes as agents of love: they wound, steal, speak and suffer
Pati: the Lord, as the first of the three Saiva Siddhanta categories (Lord, soul, bond)
light: the Lord as light (சோதி), the inner light seen within the body and mind in meditation, and the lights of sun, moon and fire he gives
devotional service to the Lord and his devotees; becoming his servant (அடிமை, வழியடிமை) by choice, as distinct from bondage
kingship; the ruler and the office of ruling
the embryo, and its forming in the womb
samadhi: the absorbed state of the yogi or jnani; also the tomb in which such a one's body is kept
silence: the stillness of speech and mind of the sage, as a state rather than a vow
nectar: in Tirumular's yoga the fluid held to flow from the head or palate, which preserves the body
nadi: a channel of breath and life in the yogic body
pervasion: the Lord's filling of all things, the elements, the worlds, the gods, the souls and the body, while remaining one and beyond them
the Lord's five acts: creating, protecting, removing, concealing and granting grace
death, as something faced or chosen
the Veda, as scripture recited and as the source of dharma
kala: a phase or digit, of the moon and of the breath matched with it; in Siddhanta also a class of the tattvas
the oblation poured into the sacred fire; the fire rite (ஓமம்)
lovers' quarrel; the sulking that love enjoys
hell, as the after-death punishment of the wicked
adhara: one of the six supports or centres in the body named in Tirumular's yoga (the chakras), pictured as lotuses rising from the root to the brow
Vedanta: the end of the Veda, taken as the knowledge in which craving ends
baseness; lack of any inner moral restraint
remembering the absent lover; constant thought
meditation: the seventh limb of eight-limbed yoga, contemplation held on light, sound or the Lord
conduct; a disciplined way of living
the heart as a separate party the lover speaks to
youth, as a stage that passes
bhakti: devotion to the Lord, and the பத்தர் (devotees) who have it
sayujya: union with Siva, the highest of the four states of release, in which the soul becomes Siva
kundalini: the coiled power, cosmic and in the body
the Agamas: the Saiva scriptures given by Siva, traditionally twenty-eight
right timing; the season for acting
evening as the hour when longing flowers
petty understanding that thinks itself wise
support; those or that on which one can lean
the cosmic egg; a world-sphere, of which there are numberless ones within the outer egg
chakra as a drawn diagram (yantra): lines and cells filled with letters and mantras for worship or rites
the assembly; those before whom one speaks
the worthy; those complete in character
tat tvam asi, 'that thou art': the Upanishadic great saying, its words தற்பதம் (that), தொம்பதம் (thou) and அசி (art) read by Tirumular as the Lord, the bound soul and their union
speech; the spoken word and its effects
purity, especially of action and means
lack of learning, as a condition of a person
learning by listening to the wise
examining and discerning before choosing or acting
bodily beauty and wellbeing, as something love gives or takes
the lingam: Siva's emblem, as the installed stone with its pedestal and as the forms it is said to be (letters, bindu and nada, Shakti and Siva, the self, the guru)
rain, as the condition of life and of virtue
conduct at odds with one's professed state; hypocrisy of the renunciant
Siddhanta: the settled conclusion, Saiva Siddhanta as the teaching and the Siddhantin who has reached it
the sun: in Tirumular both the sun of the cosmos, worshipper and form of the Lord, and the sun within the yogic body
another man's wife, named through his home
wasting of the body in longing, shown by slipping bangles and thinning arms
chariyai: the first of the four Saiva paths, outward service of the Lord in temples (cleaning, gathering flowers, singing), the path of the devotee
children, and the good of having them
impartiality; keeping to what is fair
strength, one's own and others', to be weighed
heedlessness; forgetting oneself and one's purpose
the Brahmin, defined by rite, Vedanta and conduct; in the Kural, the virtuous one
the ascetic's garb or guise: the outward marks of a holy life, true or assumed
land; realm as a living whole
reviling or slighting what is holy: the Lord, the guru, his devotees or the jnani
sanmarga: the true or good path; in Saiva usage the path of jnana, the highest of the four paths, in which the soul becomes one with Siva
holy ash, worn as Siva's emblem and armour
mudra: a seal or gesture of the hands (or of the body) used with mantra in worship and in yoga
the obligation to serve the community with one's means
the pallor of longing, spreading over a woman's skin in separation
a good done; gratitude for it
Saivism: the religion of Siva, and in Tirumular its kinds (pure, impure, path, severe pure) and the Saiva who follows it
fear, especially fear of wrongdoing as a moral faculty
stealth; taking another's goods by deceit
kiriyai: the second of the four Saiva paths, ritual worship of Siva in a form, by Agamic rite
what hurts; harm done to others
avarice; clinging to wealth when it should be used
one-sided love; love that isn't returned
flesh as food; abstention from it
testing; careful inquiry into a person
manliness; capacity to act and govern
riding the palmyra-stem horse in public to shame or force a beloved's kin
the void: the emptiness left when maya, knowledge and their traces are let go, in Tirumular three voids (முப்பாழ்) in which speech ends and the soul comes to rest
backbiting; speaking ill of someone in their absence
the grace of the eye; kindly regard, especially for those one knows
holy water; bathing at sacred rivers and tanks to remove sin, and the inner waters set against it
the span of life, as reckoned or foretold from bodily signs and counts of the breath
killing, as crime or as punishment
farming; ploughing as the base of society
dream, as a place where the absent lover can be met
space, the fifth element (also வெளி, விசும்பு), and in Tirumular the inner space of awareness and the space in Siva that the knower attains
right place; the ground on which one acts
the next world or life, for which good deeds are provision
upadhi: a limiting adjunct, of effect or of cause, that clings to the soul (and is said to cling even to the Supreme) and must be cut away for release
not coveting what belongs to others
the ruler, seen from those who serve him
concealing what one has from one who asks; refusal
the courtesan or other woman; a man's straying, as a commentators' setting
the three gunas, sattva, rajas and tamas, the qualities of prakriti; in Tirumular matched with the states of waking, dream and deep sleep
the six ends: Vedanta, Siddhanta, nadanta, bodhanta, yoganta and kalanta, the end points of six disciplines of knowledge, which Tirumular gathers into one
spying; the spy; intelligence for the state
old friendship; a bond with long-standing claims
enmity from within one's own circle
being led by a woman's will; a husband's subordination
dread; the fear a ruler instils
asana: a seated posture of yoga, the first bodily step of the eightfold discipline
the disciple, worthy (சற்சீடன்) or unworthy (அசற்சீடன்), whose ripeness decides whether the teaching is given
upasanta: the stilling or quiescence in which the traces of action and the states fall away and the soul rests in Siva
reciting the Lord's name, as a practice or as the plea itself
the graded states of release short of union: salokam (dwelling in the Lord's world), samipam (nearness to him) and sarupam (taking his form)
goodness of conduct or manner; variously justice, grace, liking
punishing; penalty as an act of rule
the liberty of intimacy; rightful claim on a friend
the eight directions, with their guardian gods and elephants, set in Tirumular's yoga as the petals of the inner lotus
Valli, the hunter girl of the millet field whom Murugan courted in a hunter's guise and wed, when a song is about that story
the sceptre; the quality of a ruler's rule, just or cruel
a goddess or spirit that afflicts; beauty as a wounding power
adhva: the six paths (tattva, mantra, varna, bhuvana, pada, kala) of Saiva Agamic teaching, through which the soul is bound and through which it is purified
a girl's going away with her lover, against her family, through the wilderness
a sacred site or shrine where the Lord dwells and is worshipped; the place itself as an object of devotion
matha: the guru's seat or monastery, where teaching and worship go on, and in Tirumular its inner counterpart in the body
an oath or vow, especially a lover's or courtesan's sworn promise of lasting union
tender regard for those in one's care
lakshana: implication, the secondary sense by which a word points beyond its literal meaning; in Vedanta, the three modes (leaving, keeping, and both) used to read the great sayings
